Title: New students welcomed by staff, faculty and seniors
NewsSummary: The incoming class of 2021 came together to attend a first-ever joint orientation.
NewsContent:
​New students in our nursing, medicine and education programmes in Pakistan received a special welcome to life at AKU in a first-ever joint orientation. 

Over 400 undergraduate and graduate students received information essential to their success at AKU and benefited from guidance from senior students, staff and faculty during the online event organised by the Student Affairs and Services office.

Commenting on the orientation, a student said: “I really enjoyed the quick responses to our questions and the two-way conversation… it was really a good start for me and for all of us.”

The online event enabled this year’s batch of students, who come from over 43 cities across Pakistan and 5 countries, to attend orientation without having to make travel arrangements, while observing public health precautions during the pandemic.

During the event, students learned how to use key services such as the library and counselling services to maintain their physical and mental wellbeing from their homes. They also received an introduction to the hybrid learning tools that they would soon be using for their studies. 

“I like that AKU focuses not just on the learning experience of students but also on [our] overall well-being,” a student noted on the feedback form after learning about the various programmes designed to facilitate every student’s needs.

All incoming students received information on student finance, guidance on using the student portal, and a walkthrough of the blended and digital learning tools available. Each programme’s students then joined a separate session covering key details about the curriculum, the philosophy and intended impact of their studies, and future career opportunities available to them. Students could interact with the presenters throughout the programme.

Current AKU students, who are unable to physically meet their peers at the moment, were also a part of the orientation. Representatives from the over 20 student-run societies and committees highlighted the opportunities available on campus and shared how they had had adjusted their routines during the pandemic. 

In a short video, students from all entities at AKU also shared words of advice, their own experiences and 
methods of coping with online learning. 

One new student remarked: “I really liked the part of the orientation when senior students shared their journey stories and their good wishes,” adding that they were “more excited for starting AKU now.”

All sessions have been recorded and uploaded on the student portal for future access and to assist those who experienced internet connectivity issues during the orientation.

While reflecting on the orientation, a student said: “I liked the way the whole session was organised in proper sequences. It made me excited to start the semester!”
